CMB power spectrum glider

The cosmic microwave background is light from 380,000 years after the Big Bang. Its ripples follow a pattern set by just six numbers. Move them and compare with what the Planck satellite measured.

Can you find the fit? The six numbers have been scrambled and hidden. Move the sliders until your blue curve runs through the Planck data. The lower panel shows how far each data point is from your curve. When you're happy, or you give up, press Check my fit.

Spectra from a neural-network emulator trained on CAMB runs (lensed, flat ΛCDM, one massive neutrino with Σmν = 0.06 eV), accurate to a fraction of a percent over the slider ranges. Data: Planck 2018 (PR3) CMB power spectra: unbinned for ℓ < 30, bins of Δℓ = 30 above. Best-fit values: Planck 2018 TT,TE,EE+lowE+lensing (arXiv:1807.06209). χ² uses diagonal errors only and ignores correlations and foregrounds, so treat it as a game score, not a likelihood.
